answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when a blinded audit finds fabricated trades or coordinated duplicate identities. A falcon monitor can flag suspicious clusters, but independent evidence must trigger penalties so honest lookalikes are not punished. The jade ledger records deposits and slashing across the forge’s market. Creating many identities then multiplies capital at risk and ties it up, making a Sybil attack costly rather than free.
